sources.entry: TYPO3 - Powerful and advanced CMS with a large community. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: TYPO3 is an open source, GPL-licensed PHP content management framework that runs on a web server with a database.
summary.what_it_does: TYPO3 is a PHP-based web content management system with a streamlined core and optional extensions that add frontend and backend functionality. It exposes an open API so developers can extend the website (frontend) and administration (backend) through downloadable or self-written extensions. The README states it requires a web server with PHP and a database such as MySQL, and that the backend is accessed through a browser. It is said to run on Apache, nginx or IIS across Linux, Windows, FreeBSD and macOS. The README points to external resources for installation, TypoScript, release notes, extension downloads, Slack chat, StackOverflow, and contributing or reporting bugs, and it describes a security contact for reporting vulnerabilities.
use_cases: build a corporate or enterprise website
manage website content through a browser backend
extend a CMS with plugins or extensions
develop custom PHP web applications on a CMS framework
run a multilingual or large content site
how_to_run: Set up a web server with PHP and a database (such as MySQL)
Follow the Installation Guide referenced in the README to set up a basic TYPO3 installation
Check INSTALL.md in the repository for detailed system requirements
notable: Content Management Framework design with a separated core and optional extensions
Open API for extending frontend and backend functionality
Extensions available from a central download platform or written in-house
Long-running community project with extensive documentation
caveats: Requires a web server with PHP and a database; setup needs some technical knowledge
README notes a degree of study and time is needed to fully understand and use it
README links to an external Installation Guide and INSTALL.md rather than full setup steps
